body:
#216, #230 and #232 applied the CONTRIBUTING rule that the marker "is removed when that changes — when the paper is refereed and published, or when the argument is formalized or independently replayed." This PR offers the same replay for R. Pinho's two asterisked certificates, $C_{86}$ (#227) and $C_{82}$ (#229), and for the Épi construction the $C_{82}$ page also asterisks — each decided from the bytes the row cites, with no code shared with the claimants' checkers (kept as text, never run). Markdown only. It touches no line that #232 touches (checked by test merges in both orders).

## $C_{86}$ — the trace-constant certificate

**What was replayed.** The certificate `cert_n1200_A11.json` at rpinho/c86-trace-certificate commit `116a58f` (sha256 `722a287b74a9…`): a step measure $\mu$ on the cells of width $1/200$ (629 nonzero cells, support $[1/20, 1037/200]$) and eleven integer polynomials $Q$ with rational weights $b_Q$. The six finite conditions the row states — the hypotheses of Smith's sufficiency criterion [Smi24] and the arithmetic of the bound — were decided by two implementations sharing no code with each other (Python: `Fraction` and its own outward-rounded series logarithm; JavaScript: BigInt rationals and an interval library):

| | condition | how | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | $d_i \ge 0$, edges increasing, support inside $[1/20, 1037/200]$ | exact | holds |
| E2 | each $Q$ primitive, irreducible over $\mathbb{Z}$, totally real; the $Q$ distinct | exact (integer roots and monic quadratic factors within the Mignotte bound; Sturm counts) | holds for all eleven |
| E3 | $\sum_Q b_Q \deg Q < m$ | exact | $0.82978\,m$ |
| E4 | $\int \log\lvert Q\rvert\,d\mu > 0$ for each $Q$ | closed form in $g(u) = u\ln\lvert u\rvert - u$ at the edges, roots enclosed to $2^{-80}$, outward rounding | every lower end $> 0$ (each $\approx 10^{-4}$) |
| E5 | $U_\mu - \sum_Q b_Q \log\lvert Q\rvert \ge 0$ on the support | adaptive bisection; cell-edge terms by their exact monotone ranges, the smooth rest by a second-order Taylor form | proved on 3,658 boxes in both implementations, smallest certified lower bound $2.3 \times 10^{-8}$ |
| E6 | $\int x\,d\mu / m$ equals the certificate's bound and is $\le 1.8117251$ | exact | $144938007612277893/79999999999994000 = 1.81172509515360954\ldots$ |

**What was not re-derived.** The extension of E5 from the support to $\mathbb{C}$ (the minimum principle), the resultant argument that makes $\mu/m$ arithmetic, and Smith's theorem [Smi24] — published mathematics, cited by the row and read, not re-proved. The replay is of the certificate's finite conditions, which is what the asterisk is about.

**Red controls**, which must come out wrong in both implementations: the densities scaled by 0.98 (a box with $f < 0$ is found), the weights scaled by 1.3 (E3), extra mass in the first cell of the support (E4 and E6), the bound lowered by $10^{-12}$ (E6), $x^2 - 3x + 1$ replaced by $(x-1)(x-2)$ and by $x^2 + 1$ (E2).

**Re-derive** from https://github.com/carlostoledo1891/cert-machine at `d9a3942b82f9b5dd174935584601065a4e660b68`:

```
node tools/replay-c86.js --check   # the JavaScript decider against the record (~2 min); the red controls must fire
node tools/replay-c86.js           # both implementations (~10 min; the Python bisection dominates)
```

Write-up: https://carlostoledo.co/reports/optconst-queue.html#c86 (§8).

**What changes:**
- The README cell for 86 reads 1.8117251 (no asterisk); the Recent-progress line of 15 Oct 2026 drops "(unverified)" and the asterisk, and one line is added in the form the earlier replays were recorded.
- On the 86a page: the summary inequality's note no longer says the bound is asterisked; the [Pin26] row loses the asterisk, its last sentence says the certificate was independently replayed [T2026c], a [T2026c] reference is added, and a contribution note.

## $C_{82}$ — the [Pin26] certificate and the [Epi26] construction

**What was replayed.** Both rows are Doche's limit-point construction [Doc01b]: integer polynomials $R_j$ with multiplicities $m_j$ and $S_i$ with rational exponents $q_i$ give, with $T(z) = z(1-z)$, $Q = \prod R_j^{m_j}$ and $\log\lvert A\rvert = \sum q_i \log\lvert S_i\rvert$,

$$B = \frac{1}{\deg Q}\Big(\log M(Q\circ T) + \int_0^1 \max\big(0, \log\lvert A\circ T(e^{2\pi i t})\rvert - \log\lvert Q\circ T(e^{2\pi i t})\rvert\big)\,dt\Big), \qquad C_{82} \le B.$$

$B$ was decided by two implementations sharing no code with each other (JavaScript: Gaussian integers for the roots and an outward-rounded interval library; Python: integers, and doubles with a priori rounding-error bounds):

| | check | how |
|---|---|---|
| X1–X3 | integer factors; denominators monic up to sign with positive integer multiplicities; exponents rational $\ge 0$; $\deg A < \deg Q$; every numerator coprime to every denominator | exact (gcd 1 modulo a prime dividing neither leading coefficient) |
| X4 | every root of every composed factor $P\circ T$ enclosed | approximations refined in Gaussian integers at $2^{-192}$ / $2^{-200}$, then Gershgorin's theorem on the Weierstrass matrix with the corrections computed exactly: every disk isolated |
| X5 | $\log M(Q\circ T) = \sum_j m_j \sum_r \log\max(1, \lvert r\rvert)$ | enclosure |
| X6 | the integral on $[0, 1/2]$, doubled (real coefficients) | dyadic panels: a zeroth-order bound from $\lvert u(t) - u(t_c)\rvert \le \pi w$, and a second-order Taylor form with $\lvert g''\rvert \le 4\pi^2 \sum \lvert w_k\rvert \lvert r_k\rvert / \mathrm{dist}^2$ |

| row | construction | $B$ (JavaScript) | $B$ (Python) | printed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Pin26] | `certificate.json` @ `69d8964` (sha256 `b33626f3…`), 2,058 roots | $[0.2534446872487,\ 0.2534446875146]$ | $[0.2534446872487,\ 0.2534446875146]$ | 0.2534449 |
| [Epi26] | `construction.json` @ BakeLab/Epi-results `97fa6a42` (sha256 `e85e26fa…`, the digest its result file names) | $[0.2535689301873,\ 0.2535689304235]$ | the same to 13 digits | 0.2535744749068227 |

Both bounds hold. The [Pin26] row's own certified value $0.25344468733\ldots$ lies inside both enclosures. The [Epi26] construction gives $0.2535689\ldots$, about $5.5\times10^{-6}$ below the printed bound — the printed number is valid and weaker than its construction gives, as the row's comment already says.

**Controls**, decided the same way: Doche (2001b)'s and Grinsztajn's constructions (as transcribed in the [Pin26] repository) give $0.2544362\ldots < 0.25444$ and $0.2536269\ldots < 0.2536331090204145$; the [Pin26] repository's own planted failure (a multiplicity doubled) is refuted. **Red controls**, which must come out wrong in both: a bar below $B$ (refuted); a numerator equal to a denominator, a non-monic denominator, $\deg A \ge \deg Q$, a squared factor (repeated roots) and an exponent written as a float (each refused at its check).

**What was not re-derived.** Doche's theorem — that $B$ bounds $C_{82}$ — is read, not re-proved; the [Pin26] README also proves it directly, and its hypotheses are the exact checks above.

**Re-derive** from https://github.com/carlostoledo1891/cert-machine at `d9a3942b82f9b5dd174935584601065a4e660b68`:

```
node tools/replay-c82.js --check   # the JavaScript decider against the record (~1 min)
node tools/replay-c82.js           # both implementations, every control (~4 min)
```

Write-up: https://carlostoledo.co/reports/optconst-queue.html#c82 (§9).

**What changes:**
- The README cell for 82 reads 0.2534449 (no asterisk); the Recent-progress line of 16 Oct 2026 drops "(unverified)" and the asterisk, and one line is added in the form the earlier replays were recorded.
- On the 82a page: the [Epi26] and [Pin26] rows lose the asterisk and their last sentence says the construction was independently replayed [T2026c]; a reference and a contribution note are added.

*AI-assisted: prepared with Claude (Anthropic) in a certified-arithmetic setting: the replay code, the record and this pull request. Every number above is read from the pinned record at the commit cited, and was re-checked against the upstream files before sending.*

comments.body:
Holding this one, with a policy change behind it rather than any objection to the work.

The asterisk-removal requests have reached seven across two accounts (#216 and #230 merged; #232, #235, #242, #243, #249 open), covering C_1a, C_1b, C_1c, C_1d, C_3b, C_3c, C_31, C_49, C_71, C_82 and C_86. Each replay is carefully documented — certificate bytes by sha256, two implementations sharing no code, red controls that must fire — and I have no reason to doubt any of them individually. The problem is structural: a marker that one party can clear across the whole repository stops distinguishing anything, which defeats the purpose of having it.

So CONTRIBUTING now says:

> **Removing an asterisk takes a second party.** Adding the marker is a reviewer's call, but taking it off is a claim that someone other than the submitter has checked the work, so it needs evidence from someone other than whoever is asking. Any one of these is enough: the paper is refereed and published; the argument is registered with a service that mechanically checks the proof against the stated theorem, such as Palomar; a maintainer signs off; or someone independent confirms the replay in the pull request or issue thread. A replay carried out by the person requesting the removal is not by itself sufficient, however carefully it is documented [...] Post the replay, and let a second party confirm it.

**What this means here.** The replay stands as posted; it just needs one of the four. The quickest routes are a Palomar registration of the construction, or someone unconnected confirming in this thread that they re-ran it and got the same enclosure. Your write-ups make that easy to do — the sha256 and the command line are already there.

I am leaving these open rather than closing them, so the confirmations can land on the existing threads.

One mechanical note: #232 is subsumed by #243, which covers the same two constants plus C_1c and C_1d. Whichever route you take, #243 alone is enough and #232 can be closed.

Thanks for the care in these; the issue is the shape of the rule, not the quality of the replays.

**Second-party replay of Pinho's $C\_{86} \leq 1.8117251$ row** (independent of the replay in this pull request).

| bound | bytes replayed | result |
|---|---|---|
| $C\_{86} \leq 1.8117251$ [Pin2026] | `cert_n1200_A11.json` @ `116a58f`, sha256 `722a287b…e53d` (as in this thread) | E1: 629 nonzero cells in [1/20, 1037/200], $m = 39999999999997/40000000000000$; E2: all 11 polynomials pass, and the page's 11 printed $b\_Q$ equal the certificate's rationals exactly; E3: ratio 0.82977960; E4: smallest in $[9.99999986901, 9.99999986902]\cdot 10^{-5}$; E5: $f \geq 5.03972\cdot 10^{-5}$ certified on all 629 cells (1,563 pieces), minimum near $x = 0.709342054$; E6: $T/m = 144938007612277893/79999999999994000 = 1.81172509515360954188\ldots$, the bound exactly |

The printed $1.8117251$ is $T/m$ rounded up.

**How.** Our own code, written from the 86a page and Smith's criterion, standard library only; it shares no code with the certificate's checkers or with earlier replays. E1, E3 and E6 in exact rationals; E2 by a mod-$p$ factor-degree sieve and an exact root-subset test (irreducible) and exact Sturm counts (totally real); E4 from rigorous logarithms (intervals at scale $2^{-128}$) at isolated roots; E5 by per-cell Taylor models with explicit remainder bounds, exact handling of each cell's edge cusps and nearby roots, and adaptive bisection. Floats only choose split points; they never decide anything. **Red controls**, all as expected: the densest cell lowered by 1% makes E5 fail; the largest weight raised by 0.1% makes E5 fail; reducible, non-primitive and non-totally-real polynomials are refused; a bound $10^{-15}$ low is refused by E6. The minimum principle and Smith's Prop. 5.15 and Thm 1.5 are theorems; we check their hypotheses.

We have no connection with any of the claimants or earlier replayers. Prepared with AI assistance (Claude, Anthropic).

On 86a, the [Kos2026] row and its note stay exactly as they are on main. Only the Pinho row and the intro sentence change. C82 is as before. The diff against main is three files, +16 −8.

Where this leaves the second-party rule:

Whether that is enough is the maintainers' call.

**Second-party replay of both $C\_{82}$ rows of this pull request.** Every printed number is an upper bound on $C\_{82}$, so it must be at or above $B$; in both rows the upper end of our rigorous enclosure of $B$ is below it.

| bound | bytes replayed | our enclosure of $B$ | printed bound minus $B\_{hi}$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| $C\_{82} \le 0.2534449$ [Pin26] | rpinho/c82-height-certificate @ `69d8964`, `certificate.json`, sha256 `b33626f3…0fce` (as on the page) | $[0.2534446873318462, 0.2534446873318463]$ | $2.13 \cdot 10^{-7}$ |
| $C\_{82} \le 0.2535744749068227$ [Epi26] | BakeLab/Epi-results @ `97fa6a4`, `zhang_zagier_c82/construction.json`, sha256 `e85e26fa…e559` (as in its `result.json`) | $[0.2535689302577047, 0.2535689302831411]$ | $5.5 \cdot 10^{-6}$ |

Both enclosures sit inside this pull request's [T2026c] intervals and agree with the page's "0.2534446873…" and "0.25356893…". Two notes: the Épi row's printed value is a valid but loose upper bound (its construction gives $0.25356893026\ldots$, $5.5 \cdot 10^{-6}$ lower, as its own `result.json` says it rounds outward), and the Épi row on the page names no commit or hash (we used the folder's only commit, whose `result.json` pins the construction's SHA-256). As a positive control, Doche's 2001 certificate (`controls/doche2001.json` in [Pin26]) gives $[0.2544361553, 0.2544361561]$, below its $0.25444$.

**How.** Our own code, standard-library Python, written from the 82a page and the certificates' own notes; it shares no code with the certificates' checkers or with other replays. The bound is $B = [\sum\_j m\_j \log M(R\_j \circ T) + \int\_0^1 \max(0, g)\,dt]/D$ with $T(z) = z(1-z)$. H1 (integer coefficients, denominators monic up to sign, $m\_j$ positive integers, $q\_i \ge 0$ rational), H2 ($\deg A < D$) and H3 ($\gcd(S\_i, R\_j) = 1$ for every pair with $q\_i > 0$) are checked exactly; every root of every composed factor is enclosed in a disc of radius at most $2^{-303}$ by Gershgorin's theorem on the Weierstrass matrix (discs pairwise disjoint per factor); $\log M$ comes from the disc moduli; the integral is enclosed on an adaptive dyadic tiling of $[0, 1/2]$ (doubled by the symmetry $g(1-t) = g(t)$), with per-root series and rigorous remainders; the final comparison is exact. Floats only seed the root iteration. **Red controls**, all as expected: a bound $10^{-13}$ below our lower end is not implied; a denominator added as a numerator is caught by H3; a doubled, non-monic denominator is refused by H1; exponents scaled so that $\deg A = D + 1$ are refused by H2. Self-tests: Jensen's formula on synthetic cases and on the real denominators, $g$ from the roots against Horner's rule on the exact coefficients at random points, a re-tiling with a 16 times tighter target overlapping, and identical results on 1 and 14 workers. What rests on mathematics: that $C\_{82} \le B$ for any certificate meeting H1 to H3 (we read the direct argument in the certificates' notes step by step; it does not depend on Doche's paper), and Gershgorin's theorem and the series bounds.

We have no connection with the claimants or with earlier replayers. Prepared with AI assistance (Claude, Anthropic).

Thank you, @arhancanli, for the C82 replay as well. With it, each of the three rows this PR touches has an independent replay in this thread.
